content.thinking:
I'm planning the dwarf's proportions and pose—about 1.3m tall, facing forward with a blunderbuss held up, and sketching out the color palette for skin and beard before building the model.

Working out the skeleton hierarchy now: hips, spine chain, chest, neck, and head joints with specific positions and parent relationships, then scaling the whole figure so head, shoulders, and helmet top land around 1.35-1.37m. Now placing the leg limbs from hips down to ankles.

Still writing leg geometry...

Still defining sole geometry...

Now I'm setting up the torso using a loft along a spine bone chain, defining width/height stations rising from hips to chest to shape the ribcage and waist taper.

For color, I'm defining the blue tunic material using a mottled cel-shaded paint for a hand-painted look, then working on the kilt tabard by lathing a skirt profile outward from the hips before adding a leather front panel with gold trim.

Shaping the skirt frustum...

Now I'm adding a belt ring and a gold buckle box with a rotated diamond decal, then working out shoulder joint placement and the rifle pose—arms held forward with the gun axis running from the stock near the chest outward.

Still defining arm positions...

bend direction [1,-1,-0.3], right elbow [-1,-1,-0.3]; checking the right arm reach is short at 0.317, well within the 0.6 combined arm length, so it's a strongly bent but valid pose. Setting up the arm chains as shoulder-elbow-wrist parented to chest, with shoulders at ±0.3 on the root, and defining sweep radii for the upper arm and sleeve cuff geometry.

Now I'm working out the material bands along the sleeve — blue fabric transitioning to a leather bracer partway down the forearm. For the hands I'm adding an oversized sphere at the wrist for the glove, plus four finger capsules curling around the gun grip, and sizing shoulder pauldron spheres in blue with gold trim.

Writing pauldron geometry...

Adding fur cuff rings at the elbow joints...

For the forearms I'll add gold-studded leather bracer bands as rings with studs, and place fur trim around the shoulder joint and lower sleeve hem instead, skipping the awkward inside-pauldron placement. Now moving to the head, starting with a skin sphere scaled to shape the face.

Working out facial features: a protruding nose sphere, a thick angry brow capsule, and eyes built from layered spheres (white, iris, pupil) positioned on the face surface using the ellipsoid's geometry to find the correct depth.

Now I'm adding rosy cheek spheres, then moving on to the beard -- a large swept shape from chin to chest using a curved path with varying radius to create volume.

I'm also splitting the beard into three braids, a central one and two side braids, each built from alternating spheres along a path with gold banding, bound to the head bone so they hang naturally past the chest.

Now I'm defining the moustache as curling capsule sweeps under the nose with tapering radii, and shaping the two side braids as paths swooping from near the jaw down to the chest with decorative beads along them.

Then I plan three braids total—center plus two sides—each built from nine alternating spheres with a tufted tip and a small gold cylinder ring near the end, all attached to the head joint even though they trail toward the chest. For the helmet, I'm sketching a partial blue dome sphere scaled and positioned at the top of the head with a limited theta sweep to form the crown shape.

Checking the geometry overlap, the helmet's lower rim sits around y=1.224 while the head sphere's brow level is at 1.248, so the brows end up tucked just above the rim and get covered by the helmet as intended.

I'm shrinking the helmet to a half-dome so the forehead peeks out below the rim, keeping brows, eyes, and a gold trim ring properly positioned without clipping into the face. Small ear spheres get tucked near the cheek area where they'll be mostly hidden by the cheek plates, and now I'm moving on to torso details.

For the chest I'm planning a darker leather vest plate with a bandolier strap draped diagonally from shoulder to hip using a curve that conforms to the torso surface, plus small pouches and a powder horn at the hip, and for the back I'm adding a bedroll cylinder and sacks draped across behind the shoulders.

I'm placing a buckled pouch at the right hip and moving the bedroll to the left hip to match the reference, adding flat leather shoulder straps, and positioning blue/gold knee guard plates by pulling the knee joint coordinate from the limb point array.

Now I'm adding greaves, a fur boot cuff ring near the ankle, and leather buckle straps lower on the leg using ring sweeps along the leg chain, then figuring out where to attach the blunderbuss -- likely as its own joint parented near the chest or held by the hand.

Setting up the gun skeleton...

Checking the shoulder-to-hand distance for the left arm, I find it exceeds the reach limit even with longer arms, so I'm repositioning the left hand closer along the gun to u=.5, which brings the distance down to a feasible 0.59.

Now I'm confirming both arm reaches work with lengths [0.32,0.32] - right arm checks out at 0.42, acceptable for a dwarf's proportionally long arms. I'm moving on to the barrel geometry, sweeping a steel tube from G(0.3) to G(0.72) with a slight radius taper, then lathing a flared bell shape at the muzzle end aligned to the gun's direction vector.

Writing shell wall profile...

For the gold mouth rim, I'm using a ring sweep around the muzzle with 14 segments at radius 0.097, oriented perpendicular to the barrel's direction, and explicitly binding it to the gun bone since the frame has no inherent joint reference.

Now I'm adding the gold decorative bands along the barrel, setting the overall gun length to extend past the hands, and defining the barrel's direction vector. For the stock, I'm sweeping a tapered profile along the barrel axis with a wood grain paint applied along the z-axis, then adding boxes for the stock butt and steel lock plate positioned along the gun.

Next I'm detailing the hammer and trigger guard using a sweep along a curved path of control points, giving it a thin steel radius, plus a small trigger box. For the barrel bands, I'm setting up a reusable ring helper function that wraps a thin gold ring around the barrel at specified points along its length.

For surface decoration, I'm considering an engraved rune or knotwork motif. Rather than risky decal placement directly on the bell shape, I'll generate an SVG knotwork texture and apply it onto flat plane geometry mounted on the gun's stock side plate, and reuse that same texture on other surfaces like the tabard front.

For the tabard itself, I'll build it as a leather panel box positioned in front of the kilt at hip height, framed with thin gold trim boxes, and layer a diamond-knot textured plane on top for decoration.

Working out the rotation direction: since the skirt flares outward going down, I need a negative x-rotation of about -13° so the bottom of the panel pushes toward +z while the top stays in. Computing the radius slope between y=.58 and y=.33 gives about 13.5°, so I'll use -13 for the panel tilt, with the panel center placed around z=.29 at y=.43. I should also work through the same logic for the back panel.

Legs emerging from under the skirt need checking — the hip starts at y=.55 and the skirt bottom sits at y=.33, so the knee (around y=.3) ends up right at the hem, which looks fine against reference. I'm shortening the skirt so its bottom is at y=.38 instead, adjusting the panel profile points accordingly and recentering the panel around y=.46.

Now I'm working out the joint hierarchy — hip root at (0,.58,0), torso spanning y=.55 to 1.06, shoulders at y=1.0 with torso half-width .28. For the spine chain I'm placing joints from (0,.58,0) up to (0,1.0,.02), with the last joint acting as the chest attachment point for the arms, making sure the parent references line up correctly across the chain.

Defining more joints...

Still placing head parts...

For the texture, I'll make a gold knot SVG pattern on transparent background, importing it as a diamond knot design with navy fill and gold outline for the panel and bell plate, setting part colors to plain white strings since the texture carries its own coloring.

I'm also designing a gold zigzag triangle border strip for the tabard hem, then considering where to place the knot emblem -- deciding to skip the pauldron due to curved surface issues and instead placing it on knee plates and belt buckle, with small gold stud spheres as an alternative pauldron decoration. I'm defining the plane geometry call with its texture, direction, and axis parameters for applying these textured parts to bones.

Now I'm setting up eye and skin coloring using Paint objects like cel and mottle blends, double-checking that only actually-used imports (THREE, createBuilder, catmull, polyline, limb, specific paints, cel, INK) are included to avoid TypeScript unused-variable errors, while skipping unnecessary ones like glow, rng, aim, and lerp.

Writing ring and hoop sweep helpers...

Shaping the beard's main mass now, sweeping a curved path down from the chin and varying the ellipse radius along the way so it tapers naturally.

Still working out hair geometry...

Now I'm figuring out the bedroll placement near the left hip, trying different cylinder rotations and axis orientations to get it angled naturally across the body rather than relying on Euler angle math directly.

Writing bedroll rod geometry...

I'm adding a hip pouch with a flap and small gold buckle, then sketching a leather backpack with buckles and coiled rope detailing for the back view, and finishing with gold trim accents like a neck collar ring and gilded pauldron edges on the tunic.

Now I'm placing a gold hoop at the skirt hem and considering how to add a subtle zigzag pattern near the bottom using a paint function based on vertical position.

For the torso, I'm defining a paint that gives a dark leather vest region across the chest while the shoulders and sides stay blue, blending between them with a jagged edge for stitched-vest look. I'll skip the diamond stitch detailing for now and move on to applying this torso paint along the drape sweep paths.

Then I'm working out a bandolier strap curving diagonally across the torso using a catmull path, giving it a slight lift and a flat box-shaped cross-section (circular fallback if the box looks off), making sure it stays within the torso bounds. I'm adding pouches as boxes sampled along the strap path, positioning each using the path's frame data at sampled points.

I'm also designing a hip belt made of leather hoops sized to fit the torso's silhouette at that height, computing the ellipse radii from the torso loft widths, then placing a gold buckle box and a diamond-textured plate on top, checking the z-offset against the torso's front curve to make sure the buckle sits correctly against the body surface.

Checking that the skirt's lathe top overlaps the belt region so there's no visible gap, then moving to the arm sleeves and wrist cuffs. For the legs, I'm setting up a hip-knee-ankle bone chain with a radius array that tapers from thigh to knee and flares slightly at the boot, plus a color band split so trousers transition into boot material partway down the shin.

Now I'm designing the foot geometry: a scaled toe box sphere, a steel toe cap, a flattened sole box, and a heel block, all attached to the ankle tip joint. I'm confirming the joint indexing works out so the leg chain has exactly three joints (hip, knee, ankle) with two spans between them.

Working out the sole box dimensions so its bottom sits flush at ground level, sinking it slightly for overlap, and placing the foot x-offsets symmetrically for left and right legs at hip and ankle. I'll still need to handle face details like ears and eyes, and figure out the hand sphere scaling for gloves.

Now I'm working out finger placement for the gripping hands around the gun stock, defining curved capsule paths for each finger wrapping from the knuckles around to the opposite side of the grip.

Still placing hand and finger coordinates...

Adding pauldron detail...

Now I'm layering a fur collar, backpack with buckled flap, a rolled blanket bedroll, and a pickaxe strapped to the back for extra character detail.

Still adding sideburns and a hair tail sweep behind the head, then placing the eyes with white sclera, blue iris, and dark pupil spheres plus brow shading.

Writing sphere geometry code...

Setting up metadata and the builder config, then defining the skin, highlight, and beard color palettes using the cel/mottle/grain texture helpers.

Still defining material colors...

Still writing torso and spine structure...

Adding knee plate geometry and boot cuff fur rings...

Setting up arm placement...

Working out the glove and wrist shape, then building finger geometry with curved sweeps for each digit, including a mirrored pass for the opposite hand's grip pose.

I'm adjusting the fingers to wrap around the stock radius near the gun's grip point, tweaking the y-offset for a better fit. Then I'm sketching out the gun's part list — stock as a tapered sweep with wood material, plus a butt ellipsoid — all attached to the gun bone.

Continuing the gun parts: I'm adding a steel barrel rod, a wood forestock sleeve, a gold band ring, and a lathe-shaped bell with a rim hoop, all positioned along the gun bone using parametric offsets.

Working out coordinates...

I'm adding a dark circle to represent the muzzle opening, then working on placing a knot engraving plane on top of the bell, trying to match its tilt and position to the bell's curved profile at that point.

Next I'm planning gold decorative rings along the barrel at a few key lengths, then moving on to the lock mechanism—steel plates on either side with a brass pan, plus a hammer joint piece.

Still placing hammer and trigger guard geometry...

I realize the right hand position overlaps the trigger guard location, so I need to shift the hand to around l=.17 and adjust the guard to sit more forward near l .02-.09, then double-check the shoulder-to-hand distance stays reasonable.

I also still need to add stock gold inlays, a ramrod under the barrel with a gold tip, and a small sight cone on the barrel top, plus any remaining hip/bedroll details before writing out the vector helper functions.

Starting to define the coordinate helper function...

Adding beard sweep geometry...

Still placing beard strands and braid curves... then I need to sort out neck positioning and head bone attachment before moving on to the helmet.

For the helmet, I'm working out cheek plate boxes with gold trim edges on either side, sized and positioned to overlap the beard sideburns naturally, plus a diamond-shaped gold nose guard rotated and positioned against the helmet's front rim curvature.

I'm sketching the dome using a partial sphere geometry with limited theta for the rounded helmet top, checking it clears the head ellipsoid underneath, and adding gold hoop bands around the base. For surface detail I'm considering a procedural zigzag paint pattern along the lower hem to give it a gold-trimmed skirt effect against the blue base color.

Now I'm defining helper functions for building the gun ring geometry, using a frame-based ring of points swept into a tube along the gun bone, and starting to write a similar arm ring helper for consistent limb attachments.

I'm also working out the bandolier strap by draping a curve across the torso surface and sweeping it into a leather tube, then placing small pouch studs along the strap at evenly spaced positions.

I'll limit the pouch placement to run from .35 to .9 along the strap so it doesn't jut out near the shoulder end, and I'm not too worried about minor collisions between the arm and torso or slightly off-surface drape points — those are close enough. With colors being a small set of flat strings, I think this is ready to write out.
